added: {{ParagraphTYSK}}If you're babysitting a child in his or her first year of life and who hasn't learned to walk yet, it's not the same as taking care of a toddler or an older child. Infants are very fragile and require special attention and care. This article will teach you all you need to know about watching infants.
[[Category:Babysitting]]
==What to Know Before Babysitting an Infant==

Parenting expert Denise Stern says it's crucial to understand safe sleep practices when babysitting an infant. Babies under 1 need to sleep on their back in a crib with no blankets or toys. Keep unsafe items, like medicine and cleaning supplies, out of reach. Learn basic CPR and have a plan ready in case of emergency.

added: If you're babysitting a child in his or her first year of life and who hasn't learned to walk yet, it's not the same as taking care of a toddler or an older child. Infants are very fragile and require special attention and care. This article will teach you all you need to know about watching infants.
[[Category:Babysitting]]
== Steps ==
===Babysitting Before Their Bedtime===

#Have a fill-in form ready for the parents. It should include parent emergency contact info, what to feed the baby, the baby's allergies, and other stuff you should know in case of an emergency.<ref>https://helpinghandsfirstaid.files.wordpress.com/2017/06/babysitters-interview-form-and-checklist.pdf</ref> You can find one online or make your own if you prefer.[[Image:Babysit an Infant Step 1 Version 4.jpg|center]]

#Check on the baby right away if the baby is crying. Crying is one of the only ways that babies can communicate their needs. If they do start crying, it's usually because they're tired; hungry; have a wet or dirty diaper; or they're feeling frustrated, scared, or bored.<ref>[v161711_b01]. 19 February 2021.</ref> It can be hard to know why a baby is crying at first. With practice, though, you may be able to tell what the baby needs just by the sounds of their cries.<ref>[v161832_b01]. 11 June 2021.</ref>[[Image:Babysit an Infant Step 2 Version 4.jpg|center]]

#*Start by checking the baby's diaper and offering them a bottle.<ref>[v161711_b01]. 19 February 2021.</ref> You can also try offering them a pacifier if they use one. However, never try to force a pacifier into a baby's mouth.<ref>[v161832_b01]. 11 June 2021.</ref>
#*If the baby is teething, offer them a teething ring.<ref>[v161832_b01]. 11 June 2021.</ref>
#*Rock or soothe the baby if they're still upset. Sometimes, babies just need to be physically comforted when they're crying.<ref>[v161832_b01]. 11 June 2021.</ref>

#Change the baby's diaper if it's dirty or wet. If the baby starts crying, check his or her diaper.<ref>[v161832_b01]. 11 June 2021.</ref> If there is poop, or if the diaper is wet, the diaper needs to be changed. Get a fresh diaper before undoing the old one. To change a diaper, get out baby wipes, a fresh diaper, and something to keep the baby occupied while you change it. Wash your hands to avoid spreading germs, dirt, and bacteria, to the baby's fragile bottom. First, undo the diaper. Second, if the baby is male, place a clean diaper over his private area. If the baby is female, make sure to wipe front to back so you don't spread bacteria. Third, wipe the baby with as many wipes as you need, making sure to get into all the creases. Last, lift the baby's feet, remove the soiled diaper, and slide on a clean one. Latch the diaper, pattern side on the front. Wash your hands again, to wash off any pee or poop and to kill germs and bacteria so that they don't spread to other places in the house. Make sure that the baby's hands and feet are clean and free of any pee or poop after the diaper change.<ref>https://www.whattoexpect.com/first-year/diapering/how-to-change-a-diaper/</ref>[[Image:Babysit an Infant Step 3 Version 4.jpg|center]]

#Give them a bottle if they're hungry.<ref>[v161711_b01]. 19 February 2021.</ref> If the baby is still crying or doesn't have a dirty diaper, that often means that the baby is hungry.<ref>[v161832_b01]. 11 June 2021.</ref> So you will have to find the bottle and heat up the milk that the mother has told you to use. Remember, use one scoop of the formula for every two ounces and shake well. Then heat. Do not heat a bottle up in a microwave--microwaves can cause pockets of scalding hot milk and leave some parts unheated. Place the bottle in a pot on the stove and heat the water. After heating up the bottle, make sure the bottle cap is securely fastened and shake the bottle well. Then squirt some of the milk onto the meat of your wrist and if the milk is too hot, continue to shake the bottle until the milk isn't too hot anymore. Once the milk is ready for the baby to drink, prop the baby up and gently stick the rubber nipple into the baby's mouth. Do not point the nipple straight down because the baby could choke. Take breaks between sips. During breaks, sit the baby up and gently pat his/her back right between their shoulder blades. The baby will usually burp.<ref>https://kidsit.com/how-to-babysit-a-baby</ref>[[Image:Babysit an Infant Step 4 Version 3.jpg|center]]

#Offer solid food to the baby if the parents ask you to. Babies shouldn't eat solid food until they're at least 6 months old. If you have been asked to feed the baby solid food, usually you will need to feed him/her cereal or baby food. If the baby food is too watery, mix in a tablespoon of baby rice, if it has been approved by the parent. Next, put a bib on the baby and place them in their high chair. Never leave the baby unattended in the chair. Fill a small spoon halfway with baby food, and gently put the spoon in the mouth. Do not force in the spoon. If it gags on the food or dodges the spoon, it is probably full.<ref>https://kidshealth.org/en/parents/feed47m.html</ref>[[Image:Babysit an Infant Step 5 Version 4.jpg|center]]

#Play with the baby. No matter when you babysit there will always be a little time for play unless it is only in the night. This should be gentle and at the baby's pace. Keep small objects away from the baby and be sure to watch what he or she puts into the mouth. The feet are okay![[Image:Babysit an Infant Step 6 Version 4.jpg|center]]
#* Hold a baby toy a few inches away from their face. Try moving the toy back and forth. Younger infants will watch the toy with their eyes, older infants will actually reach and grab the toy.

#* Dance! Cradle the baby in your arms and gently move from side to side and sway to the music. Any music will do as long as it is not loud or inappropriate. Avoid this right after eating; wait about a half an hour after eating before trying this activity.
#* Action rhymes and games are fun. Try "Hickory Dickory Dock." Move your fingers up the baby's body while you say the rhyme.
#* Pinwheels are nice. Hold the pinwheel 6 inches away from the baby's face. Blow on it and watch the pretty colors!

#* If the infant has an activity quilt that they can lay on, an activity gym, a baby bouncer, or a baby swing, lay them or sit them in one of these. Try pointing out the toys and activities, and encouraging interaction. Gently bounce or swing a baby if they are in a swing or bouncer, this calms them and helps them learn the difference between cause and effect, trust, and body awareness.

#Try singing songs or playing soft music. Music can be really soothing to babies, and it may help settle them if they're upset.<ref>[v161832_b01]. 11 June 2021.</ref> Try "Twinkle, Twinkle, Little Star" or "An Itsy Bitsy Spider." Look into the infant's eyes as you sing.[[Image:Babysit an Infant Step 7 Version 4.jpg|center]]

#Take a walk. Avoid a walk if it is over 85 degrees out, or if it is below 30 degrees. Also, avoid a walk if it is around the time when mosquitoes are high. Place the infant in a stroller and strap them in for safety. Slowly walk and push the stroller. Point out items in nature such as: "Look! There's a duck!" Let baby feel items outside such as the cold snow or tickle grass on their tummy or feet.[[Image:Babysit an Infant Step 8 Version 4.jpg|center]]

#* Read books. Books for infants should be cloth or board books to avoid infants from chewing up the pages or tearing them out. Many bright pictures with little text are usually best. When the infant starts to lose interest, stop reading, even if you are in the middle of the book, and move on to something else. Books with different textures in them are also great for babies.

#* Try mirrors! Use unbreakable mirrors made for children. Hold the mirror in front of the baby and let them see themselves for a while. Then, sit them on your lap and hold the mirror in front of both of you. Make faces such as silly, a frown, a smile, and twitching your nose.

#To bathe the baby, fill the tub up 1/4 way with lukewarm water. Then, gently lift the infant under its arms and bottom, and place it in the tub. Do not lay the baby down! Next, with a washcloth, pat on infant safe body wash. Still, be sure to get into every roll and crease. Rinse, but do not pour water over his/her face. Next, to wash the baby's head, do the same, but very, '''VERY''' gently. Rinse with a washcloth. When you are finished, dry the baby with a soft towel, and apply lotion.<ref>https://www.mayoclinic.org/healthy-lifestyle/infant-and-toddler-health/in-depth/healthy-baby/art-20044438</ref>[[Image:Babysit an Infant Step 9 Version 4.jpg|center]]
#Put on a new diaper as you did before and then put the baby's pajamas on. Let the baby drink more milk. Then pat the baby to make it burp.[[Image:Babysit an Infant Step 10.jpg|center]]
===Dealing with a Sleep Struggle If It's Apparent===

#Rock the baby gently. All babies are different, and not all like to go to sleep the same way, but most like to be gently rocked. Try holding the baby in your arms and slowly swinging the baby back and forth, or holding the baby securely while walking around with a bouncy step, or rocking in a rocking chair.<ref>[v161832_b01]. 11 June 2021.</ref> If the baby won't go to sleep, gently lift the baby up and lay the baby in its crib.[[Image:Babysit an Infant Step 11.jpg|center]]

#*Never leave a baby in its crib on its back with its bottle in its hands because the baby could choke. After the baby is asleep, sit in the baby's room with it and wait to make sure the baby will stay asleep, and that the baby's sleep environment is safe.

#*Make sure there is nothing that the baby could play within the crib. It could distract the baby and it won't want to go to sleep. Also, soft toys should never be in a crib, because a baby could suffocate. Keep big, fluffy blankets or pillows out of the crib. Babies don't really need them and they are actually dangerous. Keep bed covers away from baby's face.<ref>https://rednose.org.au/article/soft-toys-in-the-cot</ref>

#*Do not lie a baby on its tummy, ever, even if the parent tells you to. Always place it on its back. Placing it on its tummy is very dangerous, and potentially fatal. (If the baby is old enough to flip itself over on its tummy by itself, though, it's okay if he flips himself over).<ref>https://kidshealth.org/en/parents/sids.html</ref>

#Check on the baby. Keep checking on the baby as it sleeps. This is very important as it is your babysitting duty to make sure that the baby is safe, is not fussing, is not too hot or cold and does not have a dirty diaper. Baby monitoring is fine if the parents are fine with it, if they don't have a baby monitor, or grant you permission to use them, check on them every 15 minutes.[[Image:Babysit an Infant Step 12.jpg|center]]

== Tips ==
*Gently bounce the baby to relax it if it won't stop crying. Be sure you never shake the baby!
*Be sure to clean up after yourself and the baby! Parents hate coming home to a dirty house and really appreciate arriving at a clean one.
*Make sure you let them sleep enough so they won't be grumpy.
*Educate yourself! Read an article about SIDS, and know what foods can cause harm to infants.
*When a baby is upset don't worry, keep calm. Check to see if he/she needs something, like a bottle, or a toy.
*Negotiate a fair rate for your babysitting services before you agree to babysit.
*When you are rocking the baby do not force it to but try to let the babies head rest near your heart,a heartbeat can calm a baby

*When feeding the child, don't rush, always take your time with an infant. It often takes a while to feed a baby. You are being paid to babysit, which means you are being paid to be patient and to help the baby take its time.
*Keep the TV or music low volume, this may wake the baby shortly.
*Sometimes a baby will cry ''even though you did everything right.'' Don't blame yourself if the baby cries. It could be that he or she just misses his parents.
* Feed the baby ONLY what formula/food the parents have cleared. You wouldn't want to make the baby extra hyper.
*Reading a picture book to the child is a great way to keep them entertained while also exposing them to diverse ideas, such as different cultures.
*Don't underestimate the probability that a baby boy will urinate when you change his diaper. Hold the old diaper up as a shield for a minute before moving it away and quickly putting the new one on.
*When trying to calm down a baby, try distracting her with other objects.
*If you're feeling overwhelmed, don't hesitate to call the child's parents. Don't feel as if you're totally on your own or that you're a flop of a babysitter if you need advice.
*To calm a fussy baby to help him or her sleep, try putting some pink noise or nature sounds in the background.
*Make sure to keep the baby happy. If the baby gets fussy or upset, get them a toy or other comfort object like a pacifier.
*If you know the infant's parents well try to watch how they calm the child down or handle the baby.
== Warnings ==

*Remember, do '''not''' leave a baby in a room alone. You never know, he or she might just become injured. The baby is a real person whose parents care more about him or her than anything else in the world. It is tragic when a baby gets hurt because the babysitter was careless.

*Remember to '''never''' shake a baby under any circumstances. This can cause death or serious, debilitating brain injuries from which the baby will never recover. Shaking is a violent act that can happen when someone gets very frustrated, like when a baby will not stop crying.

*When you put the baby in the crib to sleep, put him or her on his or her back, not stomach.<ref>[v161711_b01]. 19 February 2021.</ref> This is especially important if the baby is congested. If the baby is congested and tends to roll over onto his or her stomach, put the baby into an infant seat or carriage that does not allow a baby to roll over.

*Be very gentle and careful with the baby. When you are picking it up, hold it gently under the arms and hold one arm under its bottom and one arm gently behind its back — also, don't forget to support his head and neck area!<ref>[v161711_b01]. 19 February 2021.</ref> Don't hold the baby under the arms for too long because this may hurt them. When burping the baby, be very gentle. If you pat its back too hard it will hurt or cause serious injury! A baby is very fragile, especially their new growing spine.

*If you ever find yourself getting very angry or frustrated at an infant, please set the baby down in a safe place, step back for a few minutes, and perhaps call for help - someone you can trust to calm you down, or the baby's parents.<ref>[v161832_b01]. 11 June 2021.</ref>

*If you're babysitting at the parents' house, make sure to check if everything is anchored to the walls, since the infant can lean and grab things, which can be dangerous.<ref>[v161711_b01]. 19 February 2021.</ref>

Next, to wash the baby's head, do the same, but very, '''VERY''' gently. Rinse with a washcloth. When you are finished, dry the baby with a soft towel, and apply lotion.<ref>https://www.mayoclinic.org/healthy-lifestyle/infant-and-toddler-health/in-depth/healthy-baby/art-20044438</ref>[[Image:Babysit an Infant Step 9 Version 4.jpg|center]]
#Put on a new diaper as you did before and then put the baby's pajamas on. Let the baby drink more milk. Then pat the baby to make it burp.[[Image:Babysit an Infant Step 10.jpg|center]]
===Dealing with a Sleep Struggle If It's Apparent===

#Rock the baby gently. All babies are different, and not all like to go to sleep the same way, but most like to be gently rocked. Try holding the baby in your arms and slowly swinging the baby back and forth, or holding the baby securely while walking around with a bouncy step, or rocking in a rocking chair.<ref>[v161832_b01]. 11 June 2021.</ref> If the baby won't go to sleep, gently lift the baby up and lay the baby in its crib.[[Image:Babysit an Infant Step 11.jpg|center]]

#*Never leave a baby in its crib on its back with its bottle in its hands because the baby could choke. After the baby is asleep, sit in the baby's room with it and wait to make sure the baby will stay asleep, and that the baby's sleep environment is safe.

#*Make sure there is nothing that the baby could play within the crib. It could distract the baby and it won't want to go to sleep. Also, soft toys should never be in a crib, because a baby could suffocate. Keep big, fluffy blankets or pillows out of the crib. Babies don't really need them and they are actually dangerous. Keep bed covers away from baby's face.<ref>https://rednose.org.au/article/soft-toys-in-the-cot</ref>

#*Do not lie a baby on its tummy, ever, even if the parent tells you to. Always place it on its back. Placing it on its tummy is very dangerous, and potentially fatal. (If the baby is old enough to flip itself over on its tummy by itself, though, it's okay if he flips himself over).<ref>https://kidshealth.org/en/parents/sids.html</ref>

#Check on the baby. Keep checking on the baby as it sleeps. This is very important as it is your babysitting duty to make sure that the baby is safe, is not fussing, is not too hot or cold and does not have a dirty diaper. Baby monitoring is fine if the parents are fine with it, if they don't have a baby monitor, or grant you permission to use them, check on them every 15 minutes.[[Image:Babysit an Infant Step 12.jpg|center]]

== Tips ==
*Gently bounce the baby to relax it if it won't stop crying. Be sure you never shake the baby!
*Be sure to clean up after yourself and the baby! Parents hate coming home to a dirty house and really appreciate arriving at a clean one.
*Make sure you let them sleep enough so they won't be grumpy.
*Educate yourself! Read an article about SIDS, and know what foods can cause harm to infants.
*When a baby is upset don't worry, keep calm. Check to see if he/she needs something, like a bottle, or a toy.
*Negotiate a fair rate for your babysitting services before you agree to babysit.
*When you are rocking the baby do not force it to but try to let the babies head rest near your heart,a heartbeat can calm a baby

*When feeding the child, don't rush, always take your time with an infant. It often takes a while to feed a baby. You are being paid to babysit, which means you are being paid to be patient and to help the baby take its time.
*Keep the TV or music low volume, this may wake the baby shortly.
*Sometimes a baby will cry ''even though you did everything right.'' Don't blame yourself if the baby cries. It could be that he or she just misses his parents.
* Feed the baby ONLY what formula/food the parents have cleared. You wouldn't want to make the baby extra hyper.
*Reading a picture book to the child is a great way to keep them entertained while also exposing them to diverse ideas, such as different cultures.
*Don't underestimate the probability that a baby boy will urinate when you change his diaper. Hold the old diaper up as a shield for a minute before moving it away and quickly putting the new one on.
*When trying to calm down a baby, try distracting her with other objects.
*If you're feeling overwhelmed, don't hesitate to call the child's parents. Don't feel as if you're totally on your own or that you're a flop of a babysitter if you need advice.
*To calm a fussy baby to help him or her sleep, try putting some pink noise or nature sounds in the background.
*Make sure to keep the baby happy. If the baby gets fussy or upset, get them a toy or other comfort object like a pacifier.
*If you know the infant's parents well try to watch how they calm the child down or handle the baby.
== Warnings ==

*Remember, do '''not''' leave a baby in a room alone. You never know, he or she might just become injured. The baby is a real person whose parents care more about him or her than anything else in the world. It is tragic when a baby gets hurt because the babysitter was careless.

*Remember to '''never''' shake a baby under any circumstances. This can cause death or serious, debilitating brain injuries from which the baby will never recover. Shaking is a violent act that can happen when someone gets very frustrated, like when a baby will not stop crying.

*When you put the baby in the crib to sleep, put him or her on his or her back, not stomach.<ref>[v161711_b01]. 19 February 2021.</ref> This is especially important if the baby is congested. If the baby is congested and tends to roll over onto his or her stomach, put the baby into an infant seat or carriage that does not allow a baby to roll over.

*Be very gentle and careful with the baby. When you are picking it up, hold it gently under the arms and hold one arm under its bottom and one arm gently behind its back — also, don't forget to support his head and neck area!<ref>[v161711_b01]. 19 February 2021.</ref> Don't hold the baby under the arms for too long because this may hurt them. When burping the baby, be very gentle. If you pat its back too hard it will hurt or cause serious injury! A baby is very fragile, especially their new growing spine.

*If you ever find yourself getting very angry or frustrated at an infant, please set the baby down in a safe place, step back for a few minutes, and perhaps call for help - someone you can trust to calm you down, or the baby's parents.<ref>[v161832_b01]. 11 June 2021.</ref>

*If you're babysitting at the parents' house, make sure to check if everything is anchored to the walls, since the infant can lean and grab things, which can be dangerous.<ref>[v161711_b01]. 19 February 2021.</ref>

added: #Check on the baby right away if the baby is crying. Crying is one of the only ways that babies can communicate their needs. If they do start crying, it's usually because they're tired; hungry; have a wet or dirty diaper; or they're feeling frustrated, scared, or bored.<ref>[v161711_b01]. 19 February 2021.</ref> It can be hard to know why a baby is crying at first. With practice, though, you may be able to tell what the baby needs just by the sounds of their cries.<ref>[v161832_b01]. 11 June 2021.</ref>[[Image:Babysit an Infant Step 2 Version 4.jpg|center]]

#*Start by checking the baby's diaper and offering them a bottle.<ref>[v161711_b01]. 19 February 2021.</ref> You can also try offering them a pacifier if they use one. However, never try to force a pacifier into a baby's mouth.<ref>[v161832_b01]. 11 June 2021.</ref>

#Give them a bottle if they're hungry.<ref>[v161711_b01]. 19 February 2021.</ref> If the baby is still crying or doesn't have a dirty diaper, that often means that the baby is hungry.<ref>[v161832_b01]. 11 June 2021.</ref> So you will have to find the bottle and heat up the milk that the mother has told you to use. Remember, use one scoop of the formula for every two ounces and shake well. Then heat. Do not heat a bottle up in a microwave--microwaves can cause pockets of scalding hot milk and leave some parts unheated. Place the bottle in a pot on the stove and heat the water. After heating up the bottle, make sure the bottle cap is securely fastened and shake the bottle well. Then squirt some of the milk onto the meat of your wrist and if the milk is too hot, continue to shake the bottle until the milk isn't too hot anymore. Once the milk is ready for the baby to drink, prop the baby up and gently stick the rubber nipple into the baby's mouth. Do not point the nipple straight down because the baby could choke. Take breaks between sips. During breaks, sit the baby up and gently pat his/her back right between their shoulder blades. The baby will usually burp.<ref>https://kidsit.com/how-to-babysit-a-baby</ref>[[Image:Babysit an Infant Step 4 Version 3.jpg|center]]

#Offer solid food to the baby if the parents ask you to. Babies shouldn't eat solid food until they're at least 6 months old. If you have been asked to feed the baby solid food, usually you will need to feed him/her cereal or baby food. If the baby food is too watery, mix in a tablespoon of baby rice, if it has been approved by the parent. Next, put a bib on the baby and place them in their high chair. Never leave the baby unattended in the chair. Fill a small spoon halfway with baby food, and gently put the spoon in the mouth. Do not force in the spoon. If it gags on the food or dodges the spoon, it is probably full.<ref>https://kidshealth.org/en/parents/feed47m.html</ref>[[Image:Babysit an Infant Step 5 Version 4.jpg|center]]

#Take a walk. Avoid a walk if it is over 85 degrees out, or if it is below 30 degrees. Also, avoid a walk if it is around the time when mosquitoes are high. Place the infant in a stroller and strap them in for safety. Slowly walk and push the stroller. Point out items in nature such as: "Look! There's a duck!" Let baby feel items outside such as the cold snow or tickle grass on their tummy or feet.[[Image:Babysit an Infant Step 8 Version 4.jpg|center]]

#* Read books. Books for infants should be cloth or board books to avoid infants from chewing up the pages or tearing them out. Many bright pictures with little text are usually best. When the infant starts to lose interest, stop reading, even if you are in the middle of the book, and move on to something else. Books with different textures in them are also great for babies.
*Make sure to keep the baby happy. If the baby gets fussy or upset, get them a toy or other comfort object like a pacifier.
*If you know the infant's parents well try to watch how they calm the child down or handle the baby.

*Be very gentle and careful with the baby. When you are picking it up, hold it gently under the arms and hold one arm under its bottom and one arm gently behind its back — also, don't forget to support his head and neck area!<ref>[v161711_b01]. 19 February 2021.</ref> Don't hold the baby under the arms for too long because this may hurt them. When burping the baby, be very gentle. If you pat its back too hard it will hurt or cause serious injury! A baby is very fragile, especially their new growing spine.

*When you put the baby in the crib to sleep, put him or her on his or her back, not stomach.<ref>[v161711_b01]. 19 February 2021.</ref> This is especially important if the baby is congested. If the baby is congested and tends to roll over onto his or her stomach, put the baby into an infant seat or carriage that does not allow a baby to roll over.

*If you're babysitting at the parents' house, make sure to check if everything is anchored to the walls, since the infant can lean and grab things, which can be dangerous.<ref>[v161711_b01]. 19 February 2021.</ref>

added: #Have a fill-in form ready for the parents. It should include parent emergency contact info, what to feed the baby, the baby's allergies, and other stuff you should know in case of an emergency.<ref>https://helpinghandsfirstaid.files.wordpress.com/2017/06/babysitters-interview-form-and-checklist.pdf</ref> You can find one online or make your own if you prefer.[[Image:Babysit an Infant Step 1 Version 4.jpg|center]]

#Check on the baby right away if the baby is crying. Crying is one of the only ways that babies can communicate their needs. If they do start crying, it's usually because they're tired; hungry; have a wet or dirty diaper; or they're feeling frustrated, scared, or bored. It can be hard to know why a baby is crying at first. With practice, though, you may be able to tell what the baby needs just by the sounds of their cries.<ref>[v161832_b01]. 11 June 2021.</ref>[[Image:Babysit an Infant Step 2 Version 4.jpg|center]]

#Change the baby's diaper if it's dirty or wet. If the baby starts crying, check his or her diaper.<ref>[v161832_b01]. 11 June 2021.</ref> If there is poop, or if the diaper is wet, the diaper needs to be changed. Get a fresh diaper before undoing the old one. To change a diaper, get out baby wipes, a fresh diaper, and something to keep the baby occupied while you change it. Wash your hands to avoid spreading germs, dirt, and bacteria, to the baby's fragile bottom. First, undo the diaper. Second, if the baby is male, place a clean diaper over his private area. If the baby is female, make sure to wipe front to back so you don't spread bacteria. Third, wipe the baby with as many wipes as you need, making sure to get into all the creases. Last, lift the baby's feet, remove the soiled diaper, and slide on a clean one. Latch the diaper, pattern side on the front. Wash your hands again, to wash off any pee or poop and to kill germs and bacteria so that they don't spread to other places in the house. Make sure that the baby's hands and feet are clean and free of any pee or poop after the diaper change.<ref>https://www.whattoexpect.com/first-year/diapering/how-to-change-a-diaper/</ref>[[Image:Babysit an Infant Step 3 Version 4.jpg|center]]

#Give them a bottle if they're hungry. If the baby is still crying or doesn't have a dirty diaper, that often means that the baby is hungry.<ref>[v161832_b01]. 11 June 2021.</ref> So you will have to find the bottle and heat up the milk that the mother has told you to use. Remember, use one scoop of the formula for every two ounces and shake well. Then heat. Do not heat a bottle up in a microwave--microwaves can cause pockets of scalding hot milk and leave some parts unheated. Place the bottle in a pot on the stove and heat the water. After heating up the bottle, make sure the bottle cap is securely fastened and shake the bottle well. Then squirt some of the milk onto the meat of your wrist and if the milk is too hot, continue to shake the bottle until the milk isn't too hot anymore. Once the milk is ready for the baby to drink, prop the baby up and gently stick the rubber nipple into the baby's mouth. Do not point the nipple straight down because the baby could choke. Take breaks between sips. During breaks, sit the baby up and gently pat his/her back right between their shoulder blades. The baby will usually burp.<ref>https://kidsit.com/how-to-babysit-a-baby</ref>[[Image:Babysit an Infant Step 4 Version 3.jpg|center]]

#Offer solid food if the baby if the parents ask you to. Babies shouldn't eat solid food until they're at least 6 months old. If you have been asked to feed the baby solid food, usually you will need to feed him/her cereal or baby food. If the baby food is too watery, mix in a tablespoon of baby rice, if it has been approved by the parent. Next, put a bib on the baby and place them in their high chair. Never leave the baby unattended in the chair. Fill a small spoon halfway with baby food, and gently put the spoon in mouth. Do not force in the spoon. If it gags on the food or dodges the spoon, it is probably full.<ref>https://kidshealth.org/en/parents/feed47m.html</ref>[[Image:Babysit an Infant Step 5 Version 4.jpg|center]]

#Play with the baby. No matter when you babysit there will always be a little time for play unless it is only in the night. This should be gentle and at the baby's pace. Keep small objects away from the baby and be sure to watch what he or she puts into the mouth. The feet are okay![[Image:Babysit an Infant Step 6 Version 4.jpg|center]]

#Try singing songs or playing soft music. Music can be really soothing to babies, and it may help settle them if they're upset.<ref>[v161832_b01]. 11 June 2021.</ref> Try "Twinkle, Twinkle, Little Star" or "An Itsy Bitsy Spider." Look into the infant's eyes as you sing.[[Image:Babysit an Infant Step 7 Version 4.jpg|center]]

#Take a walk. Avoid a walk if it is over 85 degrees out, or if it is below 30 degrees. Also, avoid a walk if it is around the time when mosquitos are high. Place the infant in a stroller and strap them in for safety. Slowly walk and push the stroller. Point out items in nature such as: "Look! There's a duck!" Let baby feel items outside such as the cold snow or tickle grass on their tummy or feet.[[Image:Babysit an Infant Step 8 Version 4.jpg|center]]

#To bathe the baby, fill the tub up 1/4 way with lukewarm water. Then, gently lift the infant under its arms and bottom, and place it in the tub. Do not lay the baby down! Next, with a washcloth, pat on infant safe body wash. Still, be sure to get into every roll and crease. Rinse, but do not pour water over his/her face. Next, to wash the baby's head, do the same, but very, '''VERY''' gently. Rinse with a washcloth. When you are finished, dry the baby with a soft towel, and apply lotion.<ref>https://www.mayoclinic.org/healthy-lifestyle/infant-and-toddler-health/in-depth/healthy-baby/art-20044438</ref>[[Image:Babysit an Infant Step 9 Version 4.jpg|center]]
#Put on a new diaper as you did before and then put the baby's pajamas on. Let the baby drink more milk. Then pat the baby to make it burp.[[Image:Babysit an Infant Step 10.jpg|center]]

#Rock the baby gently. All babies are different, and not all like to go to sleep the same way, but most like to be gently rocked. Try holding the baby in your arms and slowly swinging the baby back and forth, or holding the baby securely while walking around with a bouncy step, or rocking in a rocking chair.<ref>[v161832_b01]. 11 June 2021.</ref> If the baby won't go to sleep, gently lift the baby up and lay the baby in its crib.[[Image:Babysit an Infant Step 11.jpg|center]]

#Check on the baby. Keep checking on the baby as it sleeps. This is very important as it is your babysitting duty to make sure that the baby is safe, is not fussing, is not too hot or cold and does not have a dirty diaper. Baby monitoring is fine if the parents are fine with it, if they don't have a baby monitor, or grant you permission to use them, check on them every 15 minutes.[[Image:Babysit an Infant Step 12.jpg|center]]

===Babysitting Before Their Bedtime===

#To bathe the baby, fill the tub up 1/4 way with lukewarm water. Then, gently lift the infant under its arms and bottom, and place it in the tub. Do not lay the baby down! Next, with a washcloth, pat on infant safe body wash. Still, be sure to get into every roll and crease. Rinse, but do not pour water over his/her face. Next, to wash the baby's head, do the same, but very, '''VERY''' gently. Rinse with a washcloth. When you are finished, dry the baby with a soft towel, and apply lotion.<ref>https://www.mayoclinic.org/healthy-lifestyle/infant-and-toddler-health/in-depth/healthy-baby/art-20044438</ref>[[Image:Babysit an Infant Step 5 Version 3.jpg|center]]
===Dealing with a Sleep Struggle If It's Apparent===

#Rock the baby gently. All babies are different, and not all like to go to sleep the same way, but most like to be gently rocked. Try holding the baby in your arms and slowly swinging the baby back and forth, or holding the baby securely while walking around with a bouncy step, or rocking in a rocking chair. If the baby won't go to sleep, gently lift the baby up and lay the baby in its crib.[[Image:Babysit an Infant Step 7 Version 3.jpg|center]]

#*Do not lie a baby on its tummy, ever, even if the parent tells you too. Always place it on its back. Placing it on its tummy is very dangerous, and potentially fatal. (If the baby is old enough to flip itself over on its tummy by itself, though, it's okay if he flips himself over).<ref>https://kidshealth.org/en/parents/sids.html</ref>

#Check on the baby. Keep checking on the baby as it sleeps. This is very important as it is your babysitting duty to make sure that the baby is safe, is not fussing, is not too hot or cold and does not have a dirty diaper. Baby monitoring is fine if the parents are fine with it, if they don't have a baby monitor, or grant you permission to use them, check on them every 15 minutes.<ref>https://www.redcross.org/content/dam/redcross/atg/PHSS_UX_Content/Babysitters-Training-Handbook.pdf</ref>[[Image:Babysit an Infant Step 8 Version 3.jpg|center]]

added: #*If the baby starts crying, check his or her diaper. If there is poop, or if the diaper is wet, the diaper needs to be changed. Get a fresh diaper before undoing the old one. To change a diaper, get out baby wipes, a fresh diaper, and something to keep the baby occupied while you change it. Wash your hands to avoid spreading germs, dirt, and bacteria, to the baby's fragile bottom. First, undo the diaper. Second, if the baby is male, place a clean diaper over his private area. If the baby is female, make sure to wipe front to back so you don't spread bacteria. Third, wipe the baby with as many wipes as you need, making sure to get into all the creases. Last, lift the baby's feet, remove the soiled diaper, and slide on a clean one. Latch the diaper, pattern side on the front. Wash your hands again, to wash off any pee or poop and to kill germs and bacteria so that they don't spread to other places in the house. Make sure that the baby's hands and feet are clean and free of any pee or poop after the diaper change.<ref>https://www.whattoexpect.com/first-year/diapering/how-to-change-a-diaper/</ref>

If the baby is female, make sure to wipe front to back so you don't spread bacteria. Third, wipe the baby with as many wipes as you need, making sure to get into all the creases. Last, lift the baby's feet, remove the soiled diaper, and slide on a clean one. Latch the diaper, pattern side on the front. #*If the baby is still crying or doesn't have a dirty diaper, that often means that the baby is hungry. So you will have to find the bottle and heat up the milk that the mother has told you to use. Remember, use one scoop of the formula for every two ounces and shake well. Then heat. Do not heat a bottle up in a microwave--microwaves can cause pockets of scalding hot milk and leave some parts unheated. Place the bottle in a pot on the stove and heat the water. After heating up the bottle, make sure the bottle cap is securely fastened and shake the bottle well. Then squirt some of the milk onto the meat of your wrist and if the milk is too hot, continue to shake the bottle until the milk isn't too hot anymore. Once the milk is ready for the baby to drink, prop the baby up and gently stick the rubber nipple into the baby's mouth. Do not point the nipple straight down because the baby could choke. Take breaks between sips. During breaks, sit the baby up and gently pat his/her back right between their shoulder blades. The baby will usually burp.<ref>https://kidsit.com/how-to-babysit-a-baby</ref>

#* Take a walk. Avoid a walk if it is over 85 degrees out, or if it is below 30 degrees. Also, avoid a walk if it is around the time when mosquitos are high. Place the infant in a stroller and strap them in for safety. Slowly walk and push the stroller. Point out items in nature such as: "Look! There's a duck!" Let baby feel items outside such as the cold snow or tickle grass on their tummy or feet.

#*Make sure there is nothing that the baby could play within the crib. It could distract the baby and it won't want to go to sleep. Keep bed covers away from baby's face.<ref>https://rednose.org.au/article/soft-toys-in-the-cot</ref>

#*Do not lie a baby on its tummy, ever, even if the parent tells you too. Always place it on its back. Placing it on its tummy is very dangerous, and potentially fatal. *Educate yourself! Read an article about SIDS, and know what foods can cause harm to infants.

*When you put the baby in the crib to sleep, put him or her on his or her back, not stomach. This is especially important if the baby is congested. If the baby is congested and tends to roll over onto his or her stomach, put the baby into an infant seat or carriage that does not allow a baby to roll over.

Place the bottle in a pot on the stove and heat the water.  After heating up the bottle, make sure the bottle cap is securely fastened and shake the bottle well. == Tips ==
*Be sure to clean up after yourself and the baby! Parents hate coming home to a dirty house and really appreciate arriving at a clean one.
*When a baby is upset don't worry, keep calm. Check to see if he/she needs something, like a bottle, or a toy.
*Make sure to keep the baby happy. If the baby gets fussy or upset get them a toy or other comfort object like a pacifier.

*When feeding the child, don't rush, always take your time with an infant. It often takes a while to feed a baby. You are being paid to babysit, which means you are being paid to be patient and to help the baby take its time.
*When you are rocking the baby do not force it to but try to let the babies head rest near your heart,a heartbeat can calm a baby
*Gently bounce the baby to relax it if it won't stop crying. Be sure you never shake the baby!
*Educate yourself!  Read an article about SIDS, and know what foods can cause harm to infants.
*Negotiate a fair rate for your babysitting services before you agree to babysit.
*Make sure you let them sleep enough so they won't be grumpy.
*When trying to calm down a baby, try distracting her with other objects.
*If you're feeling overwhelmed, don't hesitate to call the child's parents. Don't feel as if you're totally on your own or that you're a flop of a babysitter if you need advice.
*Sometimes a baby will cry ''even though you did everything right.'' Don't blame yourself if the baby cries. It could be that he or she just misses his parents.
*If you know the infants parents well try to watch how they calm the child down or handle the baby.
*Keep the TV or music low volume, this may wake the baby shortly.
*Reading a picture book to the child is a great way to keep them entertained while also exposing them to diverse ideas, such as different cultures.
*Don't underestimate the probability that a baby boy will urinate when you change his diaper. Hold the old diaper up as a shield for a minute before moving it away and quickly putting the new one on.
*To calm a fussy baby to help him or her sleep, try putting some pink noise or nature sounds in the background.
* Feed the baby ONLY what formula/food the parents have cleared. You wouldn't want to make the baby extra hyper.
== Warnings ==

*Remember to '''never''' shake a baby under any circumstances.  This can cause death or serious, debilitating brain injuries from which the baby will never recover.  Shaking is a violent act that can happen when someone gets very frustrated, like when a baby will not stop crying.

*If you ever find yourself getting very angry or frustrated at an infant, please set the baby down in a safe place, step back for a few minutes, and perhaps call for help - someone you can trust to calm you down, or the baby's parents.

*Be very gentle and careful with the baby. When you are picking it up, hold it gently under the arms and hold one arm under its bottom and one arm gently behind it's back. Don't hold the baby under the arms for too long because this may hurt them. When burping the baby be very gentle. If you pat its back too hard it will hurt or cause serious injury! A baby is very fragile, especially their new growing spine.

#Have a fill in form ready for the parents.  It should include parent emergency contact info, what to feed the baby, the baby's allergies, and other stuff you should know in case of an emergency.[[Image:Babysit an Infant Step 1 Version 3.jpg|center]]
#Make sure the baby is comfortable at all times.[[Image:Babysit an Infant Step 2 Version 3.jpg|center]]

#*If the baby starts crying, check his or her diaper. If there is poop, or if the diaper is wet, the diaper needs to be changed. Get a fresh diaper before undoing the old one. To Change a diaper, get out baby wipes, a fresh diaper, and something to keep the baby occupied while you change it.  Wash your hands to avoid spreading germs, dirt, and bacteria, to the baby's fragile bottom. First, undo the diaper.  Second, if the baby is male, place a clean diaper over his private area. If the baby is female, make sure to wipe front to back so you don't spread bacteria. Third, wipe the baby with as many wipes as you need, making sure to get into all the creases.  Last, lift the baby's feet, remove the soiled diaper, and slide on a clean one. Latch the diaper, pattern side on front. Wash your hands again, to wash off any pee or poop and to kill germs and bacteria so that they don't spread to other places in the house. Make sure that the baby's hands and feet are clean and free of any pee or poop after the diaper change.

#*If the baby is still crying, that often means that the baby is hungry. So you will have to find the bottle and heat up the milk that the mother has told you to use.  Remember, use one scoop of formula for every two ounces.  Shake well.  Then heat. Do not heat a bottle up in a microwave--microwaves can cause pockets of scalding hot milk. Place the bottle in a pot on the stove and heat the water.  After heating up the bottle, make sure the bottle cap is securely fastened and shake the bottle well. Then squirt some of the milk onto the meat of your wrist and if the milk is too hot, continue to shake the bottle until the milk isn't too hot anymore. Once the milk is ready for the baby to drink, prop the baby up and gently stick the rubber nipple into the baby's mouth. Do not point the nipple straight down because the baby could choke. Take breaks between sips. During breaks, sit the baby up and gently pat his/her back right between their shoulder blades. The baby will usually burp.

#If you have been asked to feed the baby solid food, usually you will need to feed him/her cereal or baby food.  If the baby food is too watery, mix in a tablespoon of baby rice, if it has been approved by the parent.  Next, put a bib on the baby and place them in their high chair.  Never leave the baby unattended in the chair.  Fill a small spoon halfway with baby food, and gently put spoon in mouth.  Do not force in the spoon.  If it gags on the food or dodges the spoon, it is probably full.[[Image:Babysit an Infant Step 3 Version 3.jpg|center]]

#Play with the baby. At the beginning of the evening, you will have some time for play. This should be gentle and at the baby's pace. Keep small objects away from the baby and be sure to watch what he or she puts into the mouth. Feet are okay![[Image:Babysit-an-Infant-Step-4-Version-2.jpg|center]]
#* Try singing songs. Try "Twinkle, Twinkle, Little Star" or "An Itsy Bitsy Spider." Look into the infant's eyes as you sing.
#* Hold a baby toy a few inches away from there face. Try moving the toy back and forth. Younger infants will watch the toy with their eyes, older infants will actually reach and grab the toy.

#* Dance! Cradle the baby in your arms and gently move from side to side and sway to the music. Any music will do as long as it is not loud or inappropriate. Avoid this right after eating, wait about a half an hour after eating before trying this activity.
#* Action rhymes and games are fun. Try "Hickory Dickory Dock." Move your fingers up the baby's body while you  say the rhyme.
#* Pinwheels are nice. Hold the pinwheel 6 inches away from baby's face. Blow on it and watch the pretty colors!

#* If the infant has an activity quilt that they can lay on, an activity gym, a baby bouncer, or a baby swing, lay them or sit them in one of these. Try pointing out the toys and activities, and encouraging interaction. Gently bounce or swing a baby if they are in a swing or bouncer, this calms them and helps them learn the difference between cause and effect, trust, and body awareness.

#* Take a walk. Avoid a walk if it is over 85 degrees out, or if it is below 30 degrees. Also avoid a walk if it is around the time when mosquitos are high. Place the infant in a stroller and strap them in for safety. Slowly walk and push the stroller. Point out items in nature such as: "Look! There's a duck!" Let baby feel items outside such as the cold snow or tickle grass on their tummy or feet.

#* Read books. Books for infants should be cloth or board books to avoid infants from chewing up the pages or tearing them out. Many, bright, pictures with little script are best. When the infant, starts to loose interest, stop reading, even if you are in the middle of the book, and move on to something else.

#* Try mirrors! Use unbreakable mirrors made for children. Hold the mirror in front of baby and let them see themselves for a while. Then, sit them on your lap and hold the mirror in front of both of you. Make faces such as silly, a frown, a smile, and twitching your nose.

#To bathe the baby, fill the tub up 1/4 way with lukewarm water.  Then, gently lift the infant under its arms and bottom, and place it in tub.  Do not lay the baby down!  Next, with a washcloth, pat on infant safe body wash.  Still be sure to get into every roll and crease.  Rinse, but do not pour water over his/her face.  Next, to wash the baby's head, do the same, but VERY VERY gently.  Rinse with washcloth.  When you are finished, dry the baby with a soft towel, and apply lotion.[[Image:Babysit an Infant Step 5 Version 3.jpg|center]]
#Put on a new diaper as you did before and then put the baby's pajamas on. Let the baby drink more milk. Then pat the baby to make it burp.[[Image:Babysit an Infant Step 6 Version 3.jpg|center]]

#All babies are different, and not all like to go to sleep the same way, but most like to be gently rocked.  Try holding the baby in your arms and slowly swinging the baby back and forth, or holding the baby securely while walking around with a bouncy step, or rocking in a rocking chair. If the baby won't go to sleep, gently lift the baby up and lay the baby in its crib.[[Image:Babysit an Infant Step 7 Version 3.jpg|center]]

#*NEVER leave a baby in its crib on its back with its bottle in its hands because the baby could choke. After the baby is asleep, sit in the baby's room with it and wait to make sure the baby will stay asleep, and that the baby's sleep environment is safe --

#*Make sure there is nothing that the baby could play with in the crib. It could distract the baby and it won't want to go to sleep. Also, soft toys should never be in a crib, because a baby could suffocate.  Keep big, fluffy blankets or pillows out of the crib.  Babies don't really need them and they are actually dangerous.  Keep bed covers away from baby's face.

#*Do not lie a baby on its tummy, ever, even if the parent tells you too. Always place it on its back. Placing it on its tummy is very dangerous, and potentially fatal. (If the baby is old enough to flip itself over on it's tummy by itself, though, it's okay if he flips himself over).

#Keep checking on the baby as it sleeps.  This is very important as it is your babysitting duty to make sure that the baby is safe, is not fussing, is not too hot or cold and does not have a dirty diaper.   Use a baby monitor if one is provided.[[Image:Babysit an Infant Step 8 Version 3.jpg|center]]
== Tips ==
*Be sure to clean up after yourself and the baby! Parents hate coming home to a dirty house and really appreciate arriving at a clean one.
*When a baby is upset don't worry, keep calm. Check to see if he/she needs something, like a bottle, or a toy.
*Make sure to keep the baby happy. If the baby gets fussy or upset get them a toy or other comfort object like a pacifier.

*When feeding the child, don't rush, always take your time with an infant. It often takes a while to feed a baby. You are being paid to babysit, which means you are being paid to be patient and to help the baby take its time.
*When you are rocking the baby do not force it to but try to let the babies head rest near your heart,a heartbeat can calm a baby
*Gently bounce the baby to relax it if it won't stop crying. Be sure you never shake the baby!
*Educate yourself!  Read an article about SIDS, and know what foods can cause harm to infants.
*Negotiate a fair rate for your babysitting services before you agree to babysit.
*Make sure you let them sleep enough so they won't be grumpy.
*When trying to calm down a baby, try distracting her with other objects.
*If you're feeling overwhelmed, don't hesitate to call the child's parents. Don't feel as if you're totally on your own or that you're a flop of a babysitter if you need advice.
*Sometimes a baby will cry ''even though you did everything right.'' Don't blame yourself if the baby cries. It could be that he or she just misses his parents.
*If you know the infants parents well try to watch how they calm the child down or handle the baby.
*Keep the TV or music low volume, this may wake the baby shortly.
*Reading a picture book to the child is a great way to keep them entertained while also exposing them to diverse ideas, such as different cultures.
*Don't underestimate the probability that a baby boy will urinate when you change his diaper. Hold the old diaper up as a shield for a minute before moving it away and quickly putting the new one on.
*To calm a fussy baby to help him or her sleep, try putting some pink noise or nature sounds in the background.
* Feed the baby ONLY what formula/food the parents have cleared. You wouldn't want to make the baby extra hyper.
== Warnings ==

*Remember to '''never''' shake a baby under any circumstances.  This can cause death or serious, debilitating brain injuries from which the baby will never recover.  Shaking is a violent act that can happen when someone gets very frustrated, like when a baby will not stop crying.

*If you ever find yourself getting very angry or frustrated at an infant, please set the baby down in a safe place, step back for a few minutes, and perhaps call for help - someone you can trust to calm you down, or the baby's parents.

*Be very gentle and careful with the baby. When you are picking it up, hold it gently under the arms and hold one arm under its bottom and one arm gently behind it's back. Don't hold the baby under the arms for too long because this may hurt them. When burping the baby be very gentle. If you pat its back too hard it will hurt or cause serious injury! A baby is very fragile, especially their new growing spine.

*Remember, do '''not''' leave a baby in a room alone. You never know, he or she might just become injured. The baby is a real person whose parents care more about him or her than anything else in the world. It is tragic when a baby gets hurt because the babysitter was careless.

*When you put the baby in the crib to sleep, put him or her on his or her back, not stomach. This is especially important if the baby is congested. If the baby is congested and has a tendency to roll over onto his or her stomach, put the baby into an infant seat or carriage that does not allow a baby to roll over.

#* If the infant has an activity quilt that they can lay on, an activity gym, a baby bouncer, or a baby swing, lay them or sit the in one of these. Try pointing out the toys and activities, and encouraging interaction. Gently bounce or swing a baby if they are in a swing or bouncer, this calms them and helps them learn the difference between cause and effect, trust, and body awareness.

#* Take a walk. Avoid a walk if it is over 85 degrees out, or if it is below 30 degrees. Also avoid a walk if it is around the time when mosquitos are high. Place the infant in a stroller and strap them in for safety. Slowly walk and push the stroller. Point out items in nature such as: "Look! There's a duck!" Let baby feel items outside such as the cold snow or tickle grass on their tummy or feet.

#* Read books. Books for infants should be cloth or board books to avoid infants from chewing up the pages or tearing them out. Many, bright, pictures with little script are best. When the infant, starts to loose interest, stop reading, even if you are in the middle of the book, and move on to something else.

added: #*If the baby starts crying, check its diaper. If there is poop, or if the diaper is wet, the diaper needs to be changed. Get a fresh diaper before undoing the old one. To Change a diaper, get out baby wipes, a fresh diaper, and something to keep the baby occupied while you change it.  Wash your hands to avoid spreading germs, dirt, and bacteria, to the baby's fragile bottom. First, undo the diaper.  Second, if the baby is male, place a clean diaper over his private area. If the baby is female, make sure to wipe front to back so you don't spread bacteria. Third, wipe the baby with as many wipes as you need, making sure to get into all the creases.  Last, lift the baby's feet, remove the soiled diaper, and slide on a clean one. Latch the diaper, pattern side on front. Wash your hands gain, to wash off any pee or poop and to kill germs and bacteria so that they don't spread to other places in the house. Make sure that the baby's hands and feet are clean and free of any pee or poop after the diaper change.

added: #Have a fill in form ready for the parents.  It should include parent emergency contact info, what to feed the baby, the baby's allergies, and other stuff you should know in case of an emergency.[[Image:Babysit an Infant Step 1 Version 3.jpg|center]]
#Make sure the baby is comfortable at all times.[[Image:Babysit an Infant Step 2 Version 3.jpg|center]]

#If you have been asked to feed the baby solid food, usually you will need to feed him/her cereal or baby food.  If the baby food is too watery, mix in a table spoon of baby rice, if it has been approved by the parent.  Next, put a bib on the baby and place them in their high chair.  Never leave the baby unattended in the chair.  Fill a small spoon halfway with baby food, and gently put spoon in mouth.  Do not force in the spoon.  If it gags on the food or dodges the spoon, it is probably full.[[Image:Babysit an Infant Step 3 Version 3.jpg|center]]

#Play with the baby. At the beginning of the evening, you will have some time for play. This should be gentle and at the baby's pace. Keep small objects away from the baby and be sure to watch what he or she puts into the mouth. Feet are okay![[Image:Babysit an Infant Step 4 Version 2.jpg|center]]

#To bathe the baby, fill the tub up 1/4 way with lukewarm water.  Then, gently lift the infant under its arms and bottom, and place it in tub.  Do not lay the baby down!  Next, with a washcloth, pat on infant safe body wash.  Still be sure to get into every roll and crease.  Rinse, but do not pour water over his/her face.  Next, to wash the baby's head, do the same, but VERY VERY gently.  Rinse with washcloth.  When you are finished, dry the baby with a soft towel, and apply lotion.[[Image:Babysit an Infant Step 5 Version 3.jpg|center]]
#Put on a new diaper as you did before and then put the baby's pajamas on. Let the baby drink more milk. Then pat the baby to make it burp.[[Image:Babysit an Infant Step 6 Version 3.jpg|center]]

#All babies are different, and not all like to go to sleep the same way, but most like to be gently rocked.  Try holding the baby in your arms and slowly swinging the baby back and forth, or holding the baby securely while walking around with a bouncy step, or rocking in a rocking chair. If the baby won't go to sleep, gently lift the baby up and lay the baby in its crib.[[Image:Babysit an Infant Step 7 Version 3.jpg|center]]

#Keep checking on the baby as it sleeps.  This is very important as it is your babysitting duty to make sure that the baby is safe, is not fussing, is not too hot or cold and does not have a dirty diaper.   Use a baby monitor if one is provided.[[Image:Babysit an Infant Step 8 Version 3.jpg|center]]

#When you hear a knock on the door downstairs, don't open it yet. First look out the window. If you see that it's someone you don't know, don't answer it. If it's the parent, open the door.[[Image:Babysit an Infant Step 9 Version 3.jpg|center]]

added: #*If the baby starts crying, check its diaper. If there is poop, or if the diaper is wet, the diaper needs to be changed. Get a fresh diaper before undoing the old one. To Change a diaper, get out baby wipes, a fresh diaper, and something to keep the baby occupied while you change it.  First, undo the diaper.  Second, if the baby is male, place a clean diaper over his private area. If the baby is female, make sure to wipe front to back so you don't spread bacteria. Third, wipe the baby with as many wipes as you need, making sure to get into all the creases.  Last, lift the baby's feet, remove the soiled diaper, and slide on a clean one. Latch the diaper, pattern side on front.

added: *Sometimes a baby will cry ''even though you did everything right.'' Don't blame yourself if the baby cries. It could be that he or she just misses Mommy and Daddy.

*When feeding the child, don't rush, always take your time with an infant. It often takes a while to feed a baby. You are being paid to babysit, which means you are being paid to be patient and to help the baby take its time.
*If your feeling overwhelmed, don't hesitate to call the child's parents. Don't feel as if you're totally on your own or that you're a flop of a babysitter if you need advice.
*Negotiate a fair rate for your babysitting services before you agree to babysit.

*Remember, do '''not''' leave a baby in a room alone. You never know, he or she might just become injured. What would the parents think if they came home and their most prized possession were hurt thanks to a careless babysitter?

Once the milk is ready for the baby to drink, prop the baby up and gently stick the rubber nipple into the baby's mouth. Do not point the nipple straight down because the baby could choke. #*Ask the parent if the baby has any allergies and what to feed the baby and also ask the parent where the baby's bottle is located. Ask the parent if the baby has rashes or if the baby needs to bathe regularly. You also need to ask if the baby has any medicine to be taken. You have to ask the parent where the diapers are found and about how many times the baby needs to be changed per day. And most importantly - ask the parent what time the baby goes to bed. Ask the parents how the baby prefers sleeping before they leave the baby in your care.
# Make sure the baby is comfortable at all times.

#*If the baby starts crying, check its diaper. If there is stool in it, the diaper needs to be changed. To [[Change a Diaper|change a diaper]], there is one sticky strap on each side of the baby. Unstrap the diaper and get a fresh one. BEFORE STRAPPING THAT ONE ON, you must remember if the parent asked you to sprinkle baby powder or rub baby oil on the baby's behind. If instructed by the parent, do so. Then strap the new diaper onto the baby and you've changed a diaper.

#*If the baby is still crying, that often means that the baby is hungry. So you will have to find the bottle and heat up the milk that the mother has told you to use. Now, there are two ways that you can heat up a bottle. You may either take a pot and put it on the stove and put the bottle in it, or you may heat it up in the microwave. Most people prefer putting it on the stove mainly because if it's being put in the microwave, perhaps the middle region of the bottle will be cold and the top of the bottle will be scalding hot. After heating up the bottle, make sure the bottle cap is securely fastened and shake the bottle well. Then squirt some of the milk onto the meat of your wrist and if the milk is too hot, continue to shake the bottle until the milk isn't too hot anymore. Once the milk is ready for the baby to drink, prop the baby up and gently stick the rubber nipple into the baby's mouth. Do not point the nipple straight down because the baby could choke. Take breaks between sips. During breaks, sit the baby up and gently pat his/her back right between their shoulder blades. The baby will usually burp.

#*Give the baby solid food if requested. Remember if the parent requested that you give the baby a specific food. If the food is hard, usually a baby's parent wouldn't let the baby eat it. If the food is soft, still make sure that the food is chopped into little cubes or chunks so that the baby doesn't choke. Keep in mind - babies only have a few teeth, so it might be a little difficult for a baby to chew something hard such as a carrot or an apple. Make sure the food is soft. When the baby is done eating, you'll be able to tell because they will stop eating.

#Play with the baby. At the beginning of the evening, you will have some time for play. This should be gentle and at the baby's pace. Keep small objects away from the baby and be sure to watch what he or she puts into the mouth. Feet are okay!

#[[Bathe an Infant|Give the baby a bath]] if the parent asked you to. If they did ask you to, start running the bath water. NEVER leave the baby unattended in the bath tub alone. Be watching him or her at all times! To get the baby in the tub, gently lift the baby under its arms and place the baby in the tub. Don't let the baby lay on its back while in the tub. Let the baby splash around for a while. Then take a washcloth and squeeze Body Wash soap onto the washcloth. Gently caress the baby with the washcloth and make sure the baby gets washed everywhere. Remember to always dab, never scrub. If the baby starts crying, that means you're doing something that the baby doesn't like. Check where you're washing the baby - usually that's the case. Rinse the body wash when you're finished washing. Then wash the baby's hair with shampoo. But do make sure that you don't get the shampoo in the baby's eyes. It will sting the baby! If you have to, cover the baby's eyes while washing hair. Then caress the baby's hair with conditioner. After all of this has been done, make sure ALL soap is completely rinsed out. Lift the baby out of the bath tub as you did to put the baby in. THEN drain the bath water. Dry the baby's hair with a towel or a blow-dryer if suggested by the baby's guardian. If using a blow-dryer, make sure that water doesn't get near the outlets.
#Put on a new diaper as you did before and then put the baby's pajamas on. Let the baby drink more milk. Then pat the baby to make it burp.

#Pick up the baby in your arms and slowly swing the baby back and forth. This will make the baby tired and it will want to go to sleep. If the baby won't go to sleep, gently lift the baby up and lay the baby in its crib.

#*NEVER leave a baby in its crib on its back with its bottle in its hands because the baby could choke. After the baby is asleep, sit in the baby's room with it and wait to make sure the baby will stay asleep, and that the baby's sleep environment is safe --

#*Do not lie a baby on its tummy, '''ever''', even if the parent tells you too. Always place it on its back.  (If the baby is old enough to flip itself over on it's tummy by itself, though, it's okay).

#Keep checking on the baby as it sleeps.  This is very important as it is your babysitting duty to make sure that the baby is safe, is not fussing, is not too hot or cold and does not have a dirty diaper.   Use a baby monitor if one is provided.

#When you hear a knock on the door downstairs, don't open it yet. First look out the window. If you see that it's someone you don't know, don't answer it. Ask the parent if the baby has rashes or if the baby needs to bathe regularly. You also need to ask if the baby has any medicine to be taken. You have to ask the parent where the diapers are found and about how many times the baby needs to be changed per day. And most importantly - ask the parent what time the baby goes to bed.
# Make sure the baby is comfortable at all times.

#*If the baby starts crying, check its diaper. If there is stool in it, the diaper needs to be changed. To [[Change a Diaper|change a diaper]], there is one sticky strap on each side of the baby. Unstrap the diaper and get a fresh one. BEFORE STRAPPING THAT ONE ON, you must remember if the parent asked you to sprinkle baby powder or rub baby oil on the baby's behind. If instructed by the parent, do so. Then strap the new diaper onto the baby and you've changed a diaper.

#*If the baby is still crying, that means that the baby is hungry. So you will have to find the bottle and heat up the milk that the mother has told you to use. Now, there are two ways that you can heat up a bottle. You may either take a pot and put it on the stove and put the bottle in it, or you may heat it up in the microwave. I prefer putting it on the stove mainly because if it's being put in the microwave, perhaps the middle region of the bottle will be cold and the top of the bottle will be scalding hot. After heating up the bottle, make sure the bottle cap is securely fastened and shake the bottle well. Then squirt some of the milk onto the meat of your wrist and if the milk is too hot, continue to shake the bottle until the milk isn't too hot anymore. Once the milk is ready for the baby to drink, prop the baby up and gently stick the rubber nipple into the baby's mouth. Do not point the nipple straight down because the baby could choke. Take breaks between sips. During breaks, sit the baby up and gently pat his/her back right between their shoulder blades. The baby will burp.

#*Give the baby something small to eat. Remember if the parent requested that you give the baby a specific food. If the food is hard, usually a baby's parent wouldn't let the baby eat it. If the food is soft, still make sure that the food is chopped into little cubes or chunks so that the baby doesn't choke. Keep in mind - babies only have four teeth so it might be a little difficult for a baby to chew something hard such as a carrot or an apple. Make sure the food is soft. When the baby is done eating, you'll be able to tell because they will stop eating.

#[[Bathe an Infant|Give the baby a bath]] if the parent asked you to. If they did ask you to, start running the bath water. NEVER leave the baby unattended in the bath tub alone. Be watching him or her at all times! To get the baby in the tub, gently lift the baby under its arms and place the baby in the tub. Don't let the baby lay on its back while in the tub. Let the baby splash around for a while. Then take a washcloth and squeeze Body Wash soap onto the washcloth. Gently caress the baby with the washcloth and make sure the baby gets washed everywhere. If the baby starts crying, that means you're doing something that the baby doesn't like. Check where you're washing the baby - usually that's the case. Rinse the body wash when you're finished washing. Then wash the baby's hair with shampoo. But do make sure that you don't get the shampoo in the baby's eyes. It will sting the baby! If you have to, cover the baby's eyes while washing hair. Then caress the baby's hair with conditioner. After all of this has been done, make sure ALL soap is completely rinsed out. Lift the baby out of the bath tub as you did to put the baby in. THEN drain the bath water. Dry the baby's hair with a towel or a blow-dryer if suggested by the baby's guardian. If using a blow-dryer, make sure that water doesn't get near the outlets.
#Put on a new diaper as you did before and then put the baby's pajamas on. Let the baby drink more milk. Then pat the baby to make it burp.

#Pick up the baby in your arms and slowly swing the baby back and forth. This will make the baby tired and it will want to go to sleep. If the baby won't go to sleep, gently lift the baby up and lay the baby in its crib. NEVER leave a baby in its crib on its back with its bottle in its hands because the baby could choke. After the baby is asleep, sit in the baby's room with it and wait. Make sure there is nothing that the baby could play with in the crib. It could distract the baby and it won't want to go to sleep.

#When you hear a knock on the door downstairs, don't open it yet. First look out the window. If you see that it's someone you don't know, don't answer it. If it's the parent, open the door and lead the parent directly to the baby's room. When the parent says so, you may leave. But don't forget to tell the parent "thank you."
*Be sure to clean up after yourself and the baby! Parents absolutely hate coming home to a dirty house!
*Take off the baby's diaper BEFORE the baby takes a bath.

*Do not ask the parent if you will earn money for this or how much money you will get. It is rude and the parent might think that you're just babysitting for the money and the parent might lose trust in you.
